svg.title: A 44-year-old woman with Addison disease has vomited for two days with a stomach virus and stopped taking her hydrocortisone. She is drowsy. BP 82/48 lying, HR 118, temperature 38.2 °C. Sodium 128 mEq/L, potassium 5.9 mEq/L, capillary glucose 58 mg/dL.
svg.desc: Missed glucocorticoid replacement plus a vomiting illness is the classic setup for adrenal crisis, and low sodium with high potassium and low glucose fits it. Parenteral glucocorticoid and isotonic fluid are given together, and blood pressure usually starts improving within an hour or two. Holding steroids until a cortisol level returns is the error that costs lives. DKA is tempting because she is dehydrated and ill, but her glucose is 58 mg/dL, not high.
